@graph.name: How to Play RunStrict — GPS Territory Capture Running Game
@graph.description: Learn how to capture hexagonal territory tiles by running in the RunStrict GPS running game. Four simple steps from lacing up to scoring your team's split.

step.name: Start Running with GPS Tracking
step.text: Open RunStrict and start running. GPS tracks your route in real-time. Keep a 20-second moving-average pace under 12 min/km to activate hex capture mode. Anti-cheat verifies physical movement via accelerometer.

step.name: Flip Hexagonal Territory Tiles
step.text: Every ~175m hexagonal tile (Uber H3 resolution 9) you physically run through flips to your team's color — FLAME (Red), WAVE (Blue), or CHAOS (Purple). The last runner through a hex controls it.

step.name: Dominate the Map
step.text: Hexes roll up into provinces, countries, regions and continents. Zoom out and the map names the home province of the runners who hold each region, and flies the flag of the nationality that holds each continent. Climb Zone, District and Province leaderboards.

step.name: Score the Split
step.text: Every hex you cross is new ground (never run by anyone), a friendly hex (already your team's) or an enemy hex. Each team splits the same 10 points across those three: FLAME pays 3 / 1 / 6 (attack), WAVE 3 / 6 / 1 (hold), CHAOS 6 / 2 / 2 (explore). Friendly hexes pay once per hex per day; new and enemy hexes pay every run. No multipliers — the table is the whole rule.

@graph.name: RunStrict Teams Comparison
@graph.description: Compare the three teams in RunStrict: FLAME (Red), WAVE (Blue), and CHAOS (Purple). Every team splits the same 10 points across new, friendly and enemy hexes; the split is the team's doctrine.

itemListElement.name: FLAME (Red Team)
itemListElement.description: Attack doctrine. Points per hex: new ground 3, friendly 1, enemy 6. An enemy hex is the biggest single score in the game, so FLAME wins by pushing into the other side's streets. Best for runners who like to take ground.

itemListElement.name: WAVE (Blue Team)
itemListElement.description: Hold doctrine. Points per hex: new ground 3, friendly 6, enemy 1. Re-running a hex your team already holds pays 6, once per hex per day, so WAVE wins by showing up every day on the same streets, together. Best for runners who like to defend.

itemListElement.name: CHAOS (Purple Team)
itemListElement.description: Explore doctrine. Points per hex: new ground 6, friendly 2, enemy 2. A hex nobody has ever run, in any season, pays 6. Because the map persists between seasons, untouched ground only gets rarer. Best for runners who map out streets no one has run.

mainEntity.name: How does hex capture work in RunStrict?

acceptedAnswer.text: As you run, RunStrict uses GPS to track your route in real-time. Every ~175m hexagonal tile (H3 resolution 9) you physically run through flips to your team's color. The last runner through a hex holds it. Keep your pace under 12 min/km (20-second moving average) to activate capture mode. Anti-cheat uses accelerometer verification and GPS accuracy checks.
Yes, RunStrict is completely free to download and play. Available now on iOS (App Store) and Android (Google Play).

mainEntity.name: What is The Void in RunStrict?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Void is the season reset event that occurs every 40 days. When The Void arrives, all season points, rankings and team assignments are wiped and every runner picks a team again. The hex map is not reset — the land remembers its last runner's team color — so the next season starts on contested ground. Your personal run history is preserved.

mainEntity.name: What teams can I join in RunStrict?

acceptedAnswer.text: RunStrict has three teams, all chosen at season registration and locked for the season: FLAME (Red — attack: 3 points for new ground, 1 for a friendly hex, 6 for an enemy hex), WAVE (Blue — hold: 3 new, 6 friendly, 1 enemy), and CHAOS (Purple — explore: 6 new, 2 friendly, 2 enemy). Every team's split sums to 10. Friendly hexes pay once per hex per day.

mainEntity.name: Is RunStrict available on iPhone and Android?

acceptedAnswer.text: RunStrict is available now on iOS (App Store, requires iOS 15+) and Android (Google Play, requires Android 10+), with brand-new Apple Watch (watchOS 10+) and Wear OS (Wear OS 3+, Galaxy Watch 4+ / Pixel Watch) companion apps. GPS accuracy of 50m or better is required for hex capture.

mainEntity.name: How is RunStrict different from Strava or Nike Run Club?

acceptedAnswer.text: Unlike Strava or Nike Run Club which focus on personal fitness tracking, RunStrict adds a competitive territory-capture game layer to running. Every run is a strategic move in a team-based territorial war — you flip hex tiles, score by your team's doctrine, and compete on leaderboards. It combines the physical activity of a running app with the strategy of a location-based game.

mainEntity.name: How is RunStrict different from Pokemon GO?

acceptedAnswer.text: RunStrict requires actual running with pace verification (under 12 min/km), not just walking. It focuses on real athletic performance with anti-cheat measures including accelerometer verification and GPS accuracy checks. Territory is earned through physical running effort, not catching virtual creatures.

mainEntity.name: Does RunStrict drain my phone battery?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. RunStrict uses battery-optimized 0.5 Hz GPS polling (once every 2 seconds) and syncs data only on app launch, resume, and run completion. There are no persistent WebSocket connections draining your battery.

mainEntity.name: Can you cheat in RunStrict with GPS spoofing?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. RunStrict uses multi-layer anti-cheat: 25 km/h speed cap, accelerometer verification to confirm physical movement, GPS accuracy must be ≤50m, and runners must keep their pace under 12 min/km for hex capture to activate. Points are also classified and scored server-side against the previous midnight's map snapshot.
RunStrict works globally in any city with GPS coverage. The hex grid covers the entire planet. Available on iOS (App Store) and Android (Google Play) worldwide.

mainEntity.name: How does scoring work in RunStrict?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every hex you cross is classified as new ground (never run by anyone, in any season), a friendly hex (already held by your team) or an enemy hex (held by another team). Your team's scoring table decides the points: FLAME 3 / 1 / 6, WAVE 3 / 6 / 1, CHAOS 6 / 2 / 2 for new / friendly / enemy. Friendly hexes pay once per hex per day; new and enemy hexes pay every run. There are no multipliers or buffs, and the table can be tuned server-side without an app update.

mainEntity.name: Can I switch teams in RunStrict?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not during a season. You choose FLAME, WAVE or CHAOS when you register for a season and the choice is locked until The Void. Every new season starts with a fresh choice among all three teams.

mainEntity.name: How does territory ownership work beyond a single hex?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hexes roll up into provinces, countries, regions and continents. A nightly batch at midnight GMT+2 decides who holds each level. Team color always shows who holds a hex; zoomed out to region level the map labels each region with the home province of the runners who hold the most ground, and at continent level it flies the flag of the nationality that holds the most. Ties keep the previous day's owner. Per-hex owner details are never shown.
